_comment: Building specs: markets, mills, prestige buildings, mitigation infrastructure. Filled in during Phase 2.

tradingHouse._note: Unlocked at Margrave (rank 4, see data/ranks.json unlockedFeature). Income is sized so a single trading house roughly breaks even against the wealth-proportional tribute (economy.json upkeep.tradingHouseTributePercentage) at typical Margrave-era treasuries, then falls behind as wealth grows — the anti-snowball shape every other late-game building follows: bigger holdings cost more, not just earn more.

cathedral._note: Was 5000 — ABOVE the measured population ceiling of ~4,600, and above the population thresholds of every rank that requires a cathedral (Archbishop 3,000, King 3,500, Kaiser 4,200). The result was that cathedral was never once built and rank capped at Margrave. Now set just below Archbishop's own threshold, so the cathedral gates the rank rather than silently replacing it.

_mitigationNote: `mitigates` is documentation of intent; the authoritative mitigation coefficients live per-event in data/events.json (an event owns its own risk formula). Kept in sync by validateEventCatalog(), which fails if an event names a mitigation building that doesn't exist here.

dike._note: F6: flood's dedicated mitigation building — deliberately NOT shared with well/drought, so a ruler on flood-prone (wet-weather) exposure faces a real, separate investment rather than one building covering both ends of the weather distribution for free.
